contents.name: §5.2.1 Steady currents: magnetostatics as the theory of steady currents with ∇·J = 0 and time-independent fields
contents.support: The steady-current regime, the compact smooth class and the reduced pair are exactly what this definition fixes as the model's hypothesis class.

contents.name: §5.2.2 The Biot-Savart law (5.34), (5.39) and its straight-wire evaluation (5.36)
contents.support: The Biot-Savart representation for compact smooth conserved currents is the theorem; the straight-wire model is verified on the examples page.

contents.name: §5.2.2 Example 5.6, the field above the centre of a circular loop, eq. (5.38)
contents.support: The axis integral of the declared ideal loop is computed explicitly in this example.

contents.name: §5.2.2 the force of attraction between two long parallel wires
contents.support: The parallel-wire force per unit length is computed in this example from the declared ideal wire field under the adopted coupling.

contents.name: §5.3.1-5.3.2 Ampere's law in integral and differential form (5.42), (5.44), (5.55); derivation of ∇·B = 0 and ∇×B = μ0J from the Biot-Savart integral by product rules and an integration by parts (5.45)-(5.53)
contents.support: The vector-potential construction and the derivation of the magnetostatic pair are the content of this theorem, with the singular kernel handled by lem-em-newtonian-kernel-curl-identity and lem-em-smooth-newtonian-upgrade.

contents.name: §5.3.3 Example 5.7 (straight wire by Ampere's law) and Example 5.9 (infinite solenoid: field μ0nI inside, zero outside)
contents.support: Both declared axisymmetric models, their explicit fields, circulations and jumps, are verified in this example.

contents.name: §5.4.1 The vector potential: Coulomb condition ∇·A = 0 (5.61), Poisson equation and A = μ0/4π ∫ J/r dτ' (5.63)
contents.support: The Coulomb-gauge Newtonian potential and its Poisson equation are constructed in this theorem.

contents.name: §5.4.2 Magnetostatic boundary conditions: normal B continuous and tangential jump B_above − B_below = μ0K (5.72)-(5.76)
contents.support: The jump conditions at a stationary tangential sheet are derived from the weak equations in that theorem (scaffolded in batch 24); this batch uses it as the interface consistency check for the declared solenoid model.

contents.name: §5.4.3 Multipole expansion of the vector potential: dipole potential, field (5.85)-(5.87), moment forms (5.84), (5.91) and the delta-term remark (5.90)
contents.support: The controlled far-field dipole expansion with its explicit remainder, and the moment definition it consumes, are scaffolded in this batch.

contents.name: §6.1.2 Torques and forces on magnetic dipoles: N = m×B (6.1) exact for a loop in a uniform field, zero net force, F = ∇(m·B) (6.3), Problems 6.2 and 6.4
contents.support: The constant-field torque/force identities and the slowly-varying-field gradient estimate with remainders are the content of this theorem.

contents.name: §7.3.6 Boundary conditions (pillbox and loop) printed pp. 331-333
contents.support: The general stationary-interface jumps are already derived in that scaffolded theorem; the magnetostatic instances are the ones used here.

contents.name: Chapter 3 opening: steady currents, ρ = 0, ∇·J = 0, and the pair ∇×B = μ0J, ∇·B = 0

contents.name: §3.1 Ampere's law in integral and differential form (3.3)-(3.4)
contents.support: The differential form is absorbed as the magnetostatic pair of this definition; the integral form is the framework's separately scaffolded pthm-em-integral-maxwell (batch 24) and is not re-derived here.

contents.name: §3.1.1 A long straight wire: B = μ0I/(2πr)
contents.support: The explicit wire field and its circulation are verified in this example, together with the distributional source equation.

contents.name: §3.1.2 Surface currents and discontinuities (3.5)-(3.6); the infinite solenoid B = μ0IN ẑ (3.7)
contents.support: The cylindrical sheet model, its interior/exterior fields, its jump and its distributional curl are verified in this example.

contents.name: §3.2 The vector potential: B = ∇×A from ∇·B = 0, gauge freedom, and ∇²A = −μ0J in Coulomb gauge (3.8)-(3.13)
contents.support: The Coulomb-gauge Newtonian potential solving the componentwise Poisson equations is constructed in this theorem.

contents.name: §3.2.3 The Biot-Savart law (3.15) and its thin-wire form (3.16)
contents.support: The Biot-Savart representation and its declared thin-loop limit are the content of this theorem.

contents.name: §3.2.4 A mathematical diversion: the linking number
contents.reason: The linking-number discussion is topological exposition about flux linkage of closed currents; no item of this pair consumes it, and the framework's flux-linkage content belongs to the induction and gauge pairs rather than to magnetostatics in vacuum.

contents.name: §3.3.1 A current loop: far field and dipole moment m = IA
contents.support: The loop moment and its use in the far-field expansion are scaffolded here through the moment definition and the dipole theorem.

contents.name: §3.3.2 General current distributions: m = ½∫r′×J(r′) with the moment manipulations leading to it
contents.support: The volume-current moment is defined here; the controlled far-field use is pthm-em-magnetic-dipole-field.

contents.name: §3.4.1 Force between currents: parallel wires and f = −(μ0I1I2/2πd)x̂ (3.25)
contents.support: The two-wire force per unit length is computed in this example under the adopted thin-wire coupling.

contents.name: §3.4.2 Force and energy for a dipole: Taylor expansion of the field over a localised current, the vanishing of the constant term, and the moment identity ∫(B·r)J = ½B×∫r×J
contents.support: The first-order force evaluation and its remainder control are the content of this theorem.

contents.name: §3.5-3.5.1 Units of electromagnetism and the history of magnetostatics, including the SI value discussion
contents.support: The framework's units and the measured status of μ0 are fixed by the separately scaffolded def-em-si-conventions and def-em-steady-current-regime; the historical narrative carries no claim used by this pair.

contents.name: §43 Constant magnetic field: time averages, div H = 0 (43.1), curl H = 4πj/c (43.2), the vector potential and the auxiliary condition div A = 0 (43.3), ΔA = −4πj/c (43.4), A (43.5), the law of Biot and Savart (43.7)

contents.support: The torque identity (45.1) is absorbed into the constant-field torque clause of this theorem; the Larmor precession theorem itself is not consumed by this pair.

contents.support: The steady-current reduction uses the adopted equations of the separately scaffolded post-em-vacuum-maxwell and the continuity theorem pthm-em-charge-continuity; the covariant forms are not re-derived here.
